validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #57 collects seven review findings against the command-bar e2e work landed in #48/#53 (title: 'Follow-ups from #48: 7 from the review', label sdlc:planning). I re-checked all seven against the tree as it stands now rather than taking the review at its word; the review was written against the PR as it stood and #53 could have fixed something already.

WHAT REPRODUCES. F1, F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 are all still present in the source as described. F2 is the same defect as the centre of the ticket in a second file: `packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:241` attaches a `page.on('pageerror')` listener and line 266 reads the buffer, with only `toHaveURL` and two `toBeVisible()` calls between them — every one of those synchronises on the DOM, none on the CDP channel the errors arrive on. F4/F5 are `command-bar.test.ts:68-71` (the `let settleMatch` and the promise that nothing awaits before it resolves), `:77` and `:88-91` (the race). F6 is `:82` and `:103`, which still pin English, against `:105-106`, where #53 replaced #39's exact `toBe('Search pages, accounts and reports')` with `toBeTruthy()` plus `not.toBe('Command Bar')`. F7 is line 9 of the same file.

WHAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. F3 asserts a cmdk console error that does not exist. I checked cmdk@1.1.1 directly — `curl -sL https://unpkg.com/cmdk@1.1.1/dist/index.js | grep -c console` returns 0, and 1.1.1 is what the lockfile resolves (`yarn.lock:11807-11809`, declared `^1.1.1` at `packages/desktop-client/package.json:177`). Grepping the whole e2e tree for `key prop` and `Each child` returns nothing, so the false premise has no footprint in the repository at all: it lives only in the prose of the earlier work order and PR. There is no code to correct. I am recording the correction here so the next reviewer stops hunting for noise that cannot be generated, and I am dropping F3 rather than inventing a change for it. F1 is half true: the drain really did ship with no execution evidence, but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's configuration, not a defect anyone can fix inside a ticket — `.sdlc/config.yml:172` sets `verify.e2e: ""`, and `.sdlc/config.yml` is in `forbidden_paths`. What I can fix is the part that is mine: the drain's central claim was never checked by anything, so I make the test check it on every run (see below).

THE ROOT CAUSE, AND WHY THIS IS ONE TICKET. Every one of these findings is the same bug class: a buffer filled by an out-of-band CDP channel is read after awaits that synchronise on something else entirely. There are exactly two such buffers in the e2e tree — I grepped for `page.on('console'`, `page.on('pageerror'` and `pageErrors` across `packages/desktop-client/e2e/` and got the two lines above and no others — so fixing one and not the other would leave the class half-fixed and would make the two files disagree about the idiom. No production code changes: `CommandBar.tsx:301-306` already renders the hidden `RadixDialog.Title` and `RadixDialog.Description` that the test guards, and nothing in this ticket touches it.

TWO DECISIONS THE REVIEW LEAVES OPEN. F4 asks for either a justification of the race or its removal; I remove it. The race shortens a failing run by about a second and never changes the verdict — on the passing path both arms of the race wait the full 1000ms, and on the failing path both report `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — and removing it deletes `settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the non-optional `let` in one go, which dissolves F5 structurally instead of answering it with a comment. F6 asks for either the literal back or all three English literals dropped together; I put the literal back, because the file is pinned to English regardless (lines 82 and 103, and `Platform.isPlaywright` empties `availableLanguages` so e2e always renders English), so the literal costs nothing it is not already paying and restores a content check that #39 had and #53 weakened. Dropping all three is a larger, separable change that would ship on its own.

WHAT IS NEW HERE. F1 is the review's sharpest point and it is not satisfied by asking for the same control run a second time — #48 asked, and it did not happen. So instead of a comment, the test gains a probe: it emits a message matching its own warning regex at the moment it begins draining, and polls until that message is in a buffer. If the channel stops delivering promptly, or the pattern stops matching Radix's real wording, the test goes red by itself on every run. That converts a claim nobody was checking into an assertion something checks, and it re-proves the regex against the verbatim message each time instead of trusting a comment that cites a third-party tarball. The probe must be emitted AFTER `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — it matches the same pattern, so run first it would poison the buffer it is meant to be independent of.

NO RELEASE NOTE. `packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` runs from `.github/workflows/sdlc-release.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch`-only and writes notes per PR at release time. The four most recent commits here, including the two most recent test-only ones, added no file under `upcoming-release-notes/`. This PR is test-only and adds none either.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Buffers filled by `page.on('console')` / `page.on('pageerror')` are delivered over CDP out of band, so every await between attaching the listener and reading the buffer must be one that waits on the DOM. Neither test does that: `command-bar.test.ts` works around it with an over-built race whose payload (`let settleMatch`, `Promise.race`) cannot be proven to be assigned before use and buys nothing, and `reports.test.ts:241-266` does not work around it at all. Neither test proves its own drain can do its job, and #53 relaxed the description assertion without removing the English literals that made the relaxed form pointless.
validated_work_order.approach:
Two files, one idiom, no production code.

In `command-bar.test.ts`:
1. Doc comment: drop `(dist/index.mjs:288 and :304)`, keep the `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` pin and both verbatim messages, and say why the version but not the line numbers (F7).
2. Add a module-level `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holding Radix's verbatim description-warning string.
3. Extract the listener into `watchDialogWarnings(page: Page): { messages: string[] }` next to `referredText`, so the test body and the probe share one filter and one type.
4. In the test body: delete `let settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the `Promise.race([...])`; call `await page.waitForTimeout(CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS)` directly. That is the whole synchronisation point, and it removes F5 with the code rather than around it (F4, F5).
5. Keep `expect(messages).toEqual([])` immediately after the drain — unchanged, and still first so the accessibility assertions below cannot mask it.
6. After that assertion, add the probe: attach a second `watchDialogWarnings`, `page.evaluate` a `console.warn` of `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` from inside the page, then `await expect.poll(() => [...probe.messages], { timeout: CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS }).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])`. Poll, not a second fixed wait, so the cost on a healthy run is one round-trip and not another second (F1).
7. Restore `expect(await referredText(dialog, 'aria-describedby')).toBe('Search pages, accounts and reports')`, replacing `toBeTruthy()` and `not.toBe('Command Bar')` — the literal subsumes both, and the string is `CommandBar.tsx:305` read through i18next's natural-language keys at `lng: 'en'` (F6).

In `reports.test.ts`: add a `PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS` constant and a comment naming the same CDP reason, then `await page.waitForTimeout(PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS)` immediately before `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` (F2). Same idiom as the sibling file, kept local to each file as the existing `CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS` already is, rather than hoisted into a shared helper for two callers with different channel names.

Finally, run both controls once and paste both outputs into the PR body: inject a matching warning and watch `expect(messages).toEqual([])` fail; delete the drain line and watch it pass. `git status` must be clean afterwards. The probe makes the first of these self-checking from now on, but the second — that removing the drain makes the test pass — is a property of the drain's presence and is not something a test can assert about itself.

Add `const DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE = 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.'` beside `CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS`, documenting it as the verbatim string the probe emits so the pattern is re-proved against real wording each run. validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The review's seven findings are not equally real, and the ticket's own instruction — check each one before planning it, drop what does not hold up — is what separates them. F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 reproduce exactly as written and are small, precise edits. F3 does not reproduce at all: cmdk@1.1.1's published dist contains no console output, and no e2e file references such an error, so the premise has no repository footprint to correct and I drop it rather than manufacture a change. F1 is half real: the missing execution evidence is genuine, but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's config, and `.sdlc/config.yml` is forbidden to this ticket — so the remedy has to be something the test does itself. Hence the probe, which turns the drain's unverified claim into an assertion that fails when the channel misbehaves, rather than a control run nobody repeats.

The two open decisions were where the review offered a choice. F4 could be answered by justifying the race or by removing it; removal also deletes the non-optional `let settleMatch`, so it resolves F5 structurally instead of by comment. F6 could be answered by restoring the description literal or by dropping all three English literals; restoring is cheaper, loses nothing, and the English render is deterministic in e2e anyway (`Platform.isPlaywright` empties `availableLanguages`), while the locale-independent version would ship on its own. Both picks are argued above and both alternatives are recorded in `alternatives_considered` so a disagreeing reviewer does not have to reconstruct them.

One constraint shaped every acceptance criterion: nothing in CI typechecks or runs these files (`packages/desktop-client/tsconfig.json` excludes `e2e`, `verify.e2e` is empty, vitest's `include` skips the directory). Criteria about the test files' own logic are therefore `verify: test` with the exact command named, and only the app behaviour both tests guard is `verify: browser`. Writing a browser-observable criterion for a test refactor would have been theatre.
